title: Introduce FIPS OpenSSL build and automated JWK rotation for token services
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: several internal audits surfaced that some deployment artifacts and CI builds still produce non-FIPS OpenSSL binaries and that our service principal key rotation for JWK-based tokens is manual and error-prone. This ticket scopes a two-part remediation: (1) provide a FIPS-compatible OpenSSL build and CI packaging path for runtime images used by auth/token services, and (2) implement an automated JWK rotation workflow for token issuer services with tooling, runbooks, and backward-compatible key rollover support.
proposal: 1) Add a reproducible FIPS OpenSSL build pipeline in infra/ci that outputs signed, versioned artifacts. Integrate the build into our base docker images (runtime-base and auth-base) under a feature-flagged variant. 2) Upgrade JWT/OAuth libraries used by token-issuer and edge-auth to recent, security-patched releases, pin transitive deps, and add compatibility tests. 3) Implement an automated JWK rotation controller that: publishes new JWKs to the .well-known endpoint, supports dual-key verification window, rotates keys with a default TTL, and stores signing keys in KMS-backed HSM/KMS. 4) Roll out via canary on staging -> canary prod -> full prod with telemetry and alerting. Include rollback plan and migration runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible FIPS OpenSSL build artifacts appear in CI artifacts and are stored in internal artifact repo with checksums and signed metadata
runtime-base:fips and auth-base:fips Docker images are published and pass our standard smoke tests and integration tests
Token services (token-issuer, edge-auth) use upgraded JWT libraries and pass compatibility suite against existing tokens
Automated JWK rotation controller deployed to staging, rotates keys according to policy, and new keys are discoverable at /.well-known/jwks.json
Dual-key verification window is validated: old tokens remain verifiable for configured overlap period
Migration runbook and rollback steps documented in Confluence; security review completed and sign-off recorded
No regression in latency or error-rate (<=1% relative change) for token issuance endpoints during canary period
tasks: Define FIPS build configuration and select OpenSSL FIPS module version
Implement CI job that builds, signs, and publishes FIPS OpenSSL tarballs
Create Dockerfile variants referencing FIPS artifact and add base image promotion job
Audit and upgrade jwt/jose libraries in token-issuer and edge-auth (update go.mod/pom.xml as needed)
Write compatibility tests for token format, kid header handling, and revoked-key behavior
Develop JWK rotation controller and KMS integration (support Google KMS/AWS KMS HSM profiles)
Add telemetry: rotation events, key-publish latencies, verification errors, and audit logs
Prepare staging canary + prod rollout plan and runbook; coordinate with SRE and Security
Execute security review and threat model update, address findings
Run canary and collect metrics, then promote per rollout checklist
